question: When a sequence is generated by a known hierarchy, does gradient-trained self-attention learn the corresponding exact inference procedure, and in what order are the hierarchy's correlation scales acquired?

key_findings.claim: A filtration parameter creates a useful controlled family of sequence distributions that preserves single-node root-to-leaf marginals while deleting successively higher sibling correlations.
key_findings.evidence: The binary-tree generator reuses one sparse log-normal transition tensor at every level. At filtration level k, the 2^k nodes are sampled conditionally independently from the root using path-marginal transition matrices, then ordinary branching resumes below them; correlated leaf blocks therefore have size 2^(ell-k).

key_findings.claim: On the small synthetic tasks studied, trained encoder-only transformers match the behavior of belief propagation, including calibrated probabilities and predictable behavior under train-test filtration mismatch.
key_findings.evidence: For root classification and single-token MLM, sufficiently trained models approach matched-BP accuracy. Their softmax distributions have low KL divergence from BP marginals, and a model trained at k_train follows BP_k_train even when evaluated on data generated at another k, including uniformly sampled atypical inputs with greater dispersion.

key_findings.claim: Training resolves the hierarchy bottom-up: short-range correlations appear before progressively longer-range ones.
key_findings.evidence: During both supervised and MLM training, predictions transiently align with BP oracles whose filtration parameter decreases over time. The MLM out-of-sample accuracies form a staircase, while learning takes roughly 10^3 epochs rather than roughly 10 for root classification in the reported ell=4 setup.

key_findings.claim: Attention and probes are compatible with a layerwise upward message-passing implementation, but do not identify the trained model's computation uniquely.
key_findings.evidence: MLM attention matrices develop nested blocks matching correlated subtrees, and probes recover an ancestor most accurately once the corresponding encoder depth is reached. Appendix F constructs an ell-block, single-head approximation to BP by routing complementary-subtree messages and storing O(q^2) auxiliary quantities. The authors explicitly say ingredients of this existence construction were not imposed during training and it is not an exact explanation of the learned network.

key_findings.claim: The evidence is a controlled existence-and-correspondence result, not evidence that natural-language transformers generally execute belief propagation.
key_findings.evidence: Experiments use one main q=4 sparse non-ambiguous grammar, length 16 sequences, one masked token, depth-matched small encoders, and a known fixed tree. Alternate random tensors are only a qualitative robustness check. Variable topology, ambiguity, longer contexts, multi-head models, natural text, causal language modeling, and causal intervention on the proposed messages are not tested.

method.core_idea: Use a tree generator whose long-range correlations can be selectively removed, compare transformer outputs at every training stage to exact BP oracles for each filtration level, and inspect where the tree's latent variables become decodable.
method.mechanism: Generate sparse probabilistic binary trees; train vanilla encoder-only transformers on root classification or single-mask MLM; evaluate accuracy, KL, ranking, and distribution-shift correspondence against exact upward/downward BP; average attention maps; probe ancestors at each encoder layer; and provide a constructive transformer realization of BP.
assumptions: A fixed balanced binary tree and a known stationary transition tensor are adequate proxies for structured sequence data.
Non-overlapping production supports make the unfiltered root deterministically recoverable.
Matching BP predictions out of sample is strong evidence of computational equivalence.
Attention maps and decodability can localize a mechanism despite residual pathways and probe flexibility.
The qualitative results from a few q=4 grammars extend beyond those realizations.

techniques.role: Deletes selected long-range dependencies while preserving root-conditioned marginals.
Provides exact task marginals and deliberately mismatched reference computations.
Tracks which correlation scale the network's current predictions reflect.
Tests when latent tree variables become linearly/nonlinearly recoverable.
Shows that one-head ell-layer attention plus feed-forward blocks can approximate the required message recursion.

evaluations.metric: test accuracy and KL to BP marginals
evaluations.result: with sufficient labeled samples, models reach matched-BP performance and calibrated probabilities
evaluations.baseline: exact BP_k for matched and mismatched filtration levels

evaluations.setting: Single-symbol MLM on the same tree family
evaluations.metric: masked-token accuracy, KL, argmax agreement, and Spearman correlation
evaluations.result: trained models approach BP and sequentially align with less-filtered BP variants

evaluations.setting: Train-test filtration shift and uniform random sequences
evaluations.metric: prediction correspondence to the training-distribution oracle
evaluations.result: models retain BP_k_train-like behavior, with larger dispersion on highly atypical uniform sequences

evaluations.metric: averaged attention blocks and ancestor-probe accuracy by encoder depth
evaluations.result: nested attention ranges and decodability emerge in the order predicted by upward traversal
evaluations.baseline: filter depth, ancestry level, and a hand-constructed BP-compatible transformer

limitations: The primary experiments concern length-16 sequences, q=4, fixed balanced trees, and mostly one transition-tensor realization.
Sparse non-overlapping rules remove grammatical ambiguity and make unfiltered root classification deterministic.
The BP construction is an existence proof, not a parameter-level match to the trained networks.
Probes and averaged attention are correlational; activation patching or message-level causal tests are absent.
The study uses encoder-only bidirectional attention and single-token MLM, not autoregressive language modeling.
No scaling law in tree depth, vocabulary, ambiguity, model size, heads, or compute is established.
Sample-complexity behavior for the nonuniform grammar is explicitly left open.
failure_modes: A transformer can match BP outputs through a different compiled lookup or distributed computation, especially on a tiny finite grammar.
Probe classifiers may reconstruct ancestors from entangled correlates even when the main model never represents BP messages explicitly.
Averaging attention over examples can reveal tree-shaped routing that is not causally necessary on individual examples.
Variable or ambiguous parse trees can require chart-like inference and invalidate the fixed-position routing construction.
Multiple simultaneous masks break the simple leaf-evidence regime and may require materially different computation.
At greater depth, finite embedding width or insufficient layers may encourage shortcuts rather than scale-by-scale inference.
reusable_insights: Create distribution-preserving interventions that remove one dependency scale at a time, then use the intervened distributions as mechanistic probes.
Compare full predictive distributions, not only accuracy, when claiming an algorithm has been learned.
Deliberately mismatched exact oracles are useful fingerprints: matching their characteristic errors is harder to explain by task success alone.
Separate representational capacity proofs from evidence about the optimizer-selected mechanism.
Track learning against a nested family of partial algorithms to reveal curriculum-like acquisition order.
open_questions: Does the bottom-up sequence persist for ambiguous PCFGs, variable trees, causal next-token prediction, and natural-language clones?
Can causal interventions on candidate message subspaces distinguish BP from output-equivalent alternatives?
How do minimum layer count and embedding dimension scale with depth, branching factor, vocabulary, and mask density?
Can the filtration operator induce reliable curricula that improve sample or compute efficiency?
What predicts the training time at which each dependency radius is acquired?
Do attention-free recurrent/state-space models learn the same inference algorithm with different internal organization?

competitive_landscape.title: Do Transformers Parse while Predicting the Masked Word?
competitive_landscape.relationship: Closest prior constructive and probing study
competitive_landscape.difference: Zhao et al. construct approximate inside-outside parsing for an ambiguous PCFG with many layers and heads and probe pretrained models; this paper fixes tree topology and introduces filtration to expose training order and a much smaller single-head BP realization.

competitive_landscape.title: How Deep Neural Networks Learn Compositional Data: The Random Hierarchy Model
competitive_landscape.difference: The Random Hierarchy Model studies sample complexity and invariant representations across architectures with layer-dependent uniform rules; this paper uses nonuniform stationary transition probabilities and exact BP fingerprints to interpret transformer dynamics.

competitive_landscape.title: A Distributional Simplicity Bias in the Learning Dynamics of Transformers
competitive_landscape.difference: Rende et al. build maximum-entropy clones preserving token interactions up to an order and find low-order-to-high-order acquisition on natural-language data; hierarchical filtering instead controls spatial tree depth and supplies an exact algorithmic oracle.

competitive_landscape.title: Constrained Belief Updates Explain Geometric Structures in Transformer Representations
competitive_landscape.difference: Piotrowski et al. derive architecture-constrained Bayesian updates and detailed residual/attention geometry for HMM next-token prediction; this paper targets exact tree BP and the temporal acquisition of hierarchy levels, with less parameter-level causal specificity.

competitive_landscape.title: Unraveling Syntax: How Language Models Learn Context-Free Grammars
competitive_landscape.difference: Schulz et al. vary grammar complexity, recursion, and subgrammar structure and report parallel subgrammar loss reduction plus failures at depth, challenging a universal bottom-up acquisition story; this paper isolates dependency radius on a fixed tree and observes a clean sequential staircase.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: Hierarchical filtering reveals that transformers progressively reconstruct correlation scales and converge to a plausible belief-propagation implementation for classification and MLM.
novelty_assessment.evidence: Matched/mismatched oracle prediction traces, full-distribution agreement, nested attention maps, layerwise ancestor probes, and an explicit ell-layer construction support the claim.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The distinctive contribution is the filtration-plus-oracle fingerprint for learning dynamics. It substantially strengthens a BP interpretation on this toy family, but output agreement, attention, and probing still fall short of identifying the trained circuit, and later PCFG work indicates the acquisition order is sensitive to task and grammar structure.

reviewer_notes: Read all 17 pages, including the exact BP equations, robustness appendices, architecture details, and complete constructive implementation. Competitors were checked in primary arXiv, ACL, NeurIPS, OpenReview, and PMLR records on 2026-08-23.
